best_for: Windows developers and DBAs who juggle MariaDB, MySQL, SQL Server and PostgreSQL servers and want one small free client with SSH tunnels built in.

points.title: One client for many engines
points.text: It connects to MariaDB, MySQL, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Interbase, Firebird, ProxySQL and Redshift. Several connections can sit in one window, each with its own SSH tunnel or SSL settings.

points.title: Free under the GPL
points.text: HeidiSQL is open source under the GNU GPL. There is no paid edition; the site asks for an optional donation. If downloads fail to start, the download page says an ad blocker may be in the way.

points.title: Windows 11 first
points.text: The help page says it runs well on Windows 11, while Windows 7, 8 and 10 work with some minor issues. Windows on Arm runs the x64 build through emulation, since there is no native Arm64 Windows build.

points.title: Some drivers need a runtime
points.text: A few database drivers on Windows need the Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable. Install it first if a connection type refuses to load.

points.title: Native Linux and Mac builds exist
points.text: Recent releases also come as native Linux packages (.deb, RPM, Flatpak, tarballs) and a macOS app built with Lazarus. The Mac build runs only on Apple silicon, so Intel Macs are left out. This page lists the Windows builds only.

points.title: Wine is not the way
points.text: The project calls running the Windows build under Wine quite unstable and points Linux users to the native build instead.

points.title: Portable mode keeps settings in a file
points.text: The portable zip stores settings in portable_settings.txt next to the program. When you move to a newer portable copy, carry that file over or the session list starts empty.

points.title: Installer scope and history
points.text: The Windows installer can install for the current user or for all users, in x64 only. This listing keeps 26 Windows versions, which helps if a new release breaks a workflow.
